bandReport.notes: Phone photos, read whole. p22 opens with the INTELLIGENCE heading and Q101 (no GK tail). Q150 ends on p30, so p31 was not opened. Several pages are cut at the RIGHT edge (binding/crop), losing the last word or two of some English lines; those words were restored from the Hindi line of the same item and the visible fragment: Q102 'How will Aru[n be] coded' (Hindi अरुण), Q103 'is writ[ten as]', Q106 'grandfath[er]. [How is]', Q113 'from the ans[wer] set', Q115 'then East w[ill] become', Q117 "'CHAIR' is written as 'RI[AHC]'" (Hindi gives RIAHC), Q118 'in common a[mong] themselves', Q125/Q147 'eight frien[ds]', 'Ja[nvi]', 'taller th[an] Atul', Q135 'football and cric[ket]', 'basketball and foo[tball]', Q136 'English Alpha[bet]', Q138 'East, and co[mes] to a crossing', 'the hosp[ital]', Q139 'a certain com[mon] relationship', Q148 'What is [the code] number of' (Hindi का कोड नंबर). Item numbers 110-112 (p23), 119 (p25, top-left corner cut), 131-134, 141-145 have their leading digit(s) cut at the left edge; numbers assigned by sequence. Q119's number is not visible at all. Q123: at photo resolution the printed + and ÷ signs are hard to tell apart; read as 'If + means ÷, × means −, ÷ means × and − means +, then 15 + 3 × 4 ÷ 2 − 3 = ?' (flagged). Q143: the candidate wrote letters into the blanks of the letter series; blank positions read from the gaps as '_OPQ N_PQ NO_Q NOP_' (flagged). Q144 has no instruction line and no Hindi line in print. Q128: the candidate drew numbers (and possibly extra strokes) inside the triangle figure; the crop of the figure should be checked for pen lines before use. Q133: the Hindi and English differ (Hindi: one day after the day after tomorrow is Sunday; which day was one day before the day after tomorrow); English transcribed as printed. Q110 and Q135 share the same four premises with different final questions; Q125 and Q147 share the same height premises with different final questions; kept whole in each stem (not a printed set). All highlights, ticks, strikes, underlines and handwriting ignored.
